description: A self-contained Earth-centered orbital mechanics sandbox. Start in a circular low Earth orbit, choose a prograde, retrograde, or radial impulse, preview the osculating conic, and play or step the numerically integrated flight while watching live orbital telemetry.

repairs: The first mechanics-test run used an inaccurate expected Hohmann departure value near 2421 m/s. The implementation computed 2393.761554 m/s for 420 km altitude to a 35,786 km GEO altitude; corrected the test reference to 2394 m/s with a 1% tolerance. No physics implementation change was needed.

An added half-transfer propagation test initially required <1e-6 relative arrival-radius error. The 5 s velocity-Verlet run measured 2.7854211723696736e-5 over the roughly 5.29-hour transfer. Kept the browser-friendly 5 s step and set a still-tight <5e-5 test tolerance; exact predicted conic remains analytic while the flown trail is numerical.

The first Vite check wrapper tried to iterate build()'s return value after write:false; Vite had logged a successful build, but the wrapper raised a TypeError. Reran verification by awaiting build() without assuming a return shape; the isolated build then exited successfully.
assumptions: Planar inertial motion about a fixed point-mass Earth with μ = 3.986004418e14 m^3/s^2 and a spherical 6,371,000 m impact boundary.

Initial conditions are circular Earth orbits at a selectable 200–2000 km altitude. Maneuvers are instantaneous impulses; aim is measured from prograde toward radial-out, and a negative signed delta-v reverses the aim vector.
Predicted orbit curves are sampled from exact two-body osculating conic elements. Flown trajectories use fixed 5-second velocity-Verlet steps and add trail samples every 60 simulated seconds.

GEO altitude is 35,786 km above the selected mean-radius boundary. The Reach GEO preset executes only the departure burn; a second burn is needed to circularize. Escape preset adds 25 m/s above local escape speed. Reentry preset targets a perigee 50 km beneath the spherical boundary.
limitations: No atmosphere, drag, Earth oblateness, Moon or Sun gravity, finite-duration thrust, changing spacecraft mass, or rotating-Earth launch coordinates.
The point-mass model is educational and does not provide operational navigation or mission-design guidance.

No browser/local-host QA was performed, as the run scaffold explicitly prohibits browser localhost access. Appearance, live interaction behavior, accessibility in actual browsers, and runtime performance remain unverified pending separate review.
unknowns: Actual browser rendering, responsive layout, device-pixel-ratio behavior, and performance at the fastest time scale have not been observed.
Only syntax, isolated production bundling, and direct numerical tests were run; there is no automated DOM interaction test.
